s:
With reference to the qualifications prescribed for appointment as the Attorney General for India, consider the following statements:
1. The person must be a citizen of India.
2. The person must have been a Judge of a High Court for at least five years, or an advocate of a High Court for at least ten years.
3. An eminent jurist may also be appointed if the President considers the person suitable.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Article 76 requires the Attorney General to satisfy the qualifications for appointment as a Supreme Court Judge, including the stated judicial, advocacy or eminent-jurist qualifications.
tq: Combine the constitutional qualification routes and check whether the broader category of eminent jurist is included.
sec: Attorney General - Article 76, appointment, qualification, term, removal

s: In relation to the resignation of the Attorney General for India, which one of the following is correct?
o: The resignation is addressed to the President
The resignation is addressed to the Union Law Minister
The resignation is addressed to the Chief Justice of India
The resignation is addressed to the Prime Minister
x: The Attorney General resigns by addressing the resignation to the President.
tq: Use the appointing authority and the resignation authority as a paired constitutional relationship.
sec: Attorney General - Article 76, appointment, qualification, term, removal

s: Which of the following statements regarding the removal of the Attorney General for India is correct?
o: Removal can be ordered only by the Supreme Court
Removal requires impeachment by both Houses of Parliament
The Constitution specifies detailed grounds and a special removal procedure
The Constitution does not specify grounds or a separate removal procedure; the office is held during the President's pleasure
x: The Constitution does not prescribe specific grounds or a special procedure for removal of the Attorney General. The office is held during the pleasure of the President.
tq: Distinguish an office held during pleasure from constitutional offices having a prescribed removal procedure.
sec: Attorney General - Article 76, appointment, qualification, term, removal

s: The convention that the Attorney General resigns when the Council of Ministers resigns or is replaced is primarily related to the fact that the Attorney General is appointed on the advice of the:
x: The Attorney General is appointed by the President on the advice of the Council of Ministers. By convention, the Attorney General resigns when that Council resigns or is replaced.
tq: Link the convention to the political advice underlying the appointment rather than to the formal appointing authority alone.
sec: Attorney General - Article 76, appointment, qualification, term, removal

s: Who determines the remuneration of the Attorney General for India?
x: The remuneration of the Attorney General is determined by the President.
tq: Apply the authority-power test: identify which constitutional authority is assigned the remuneration decision.
sec: Attorney General - Article 76, appointment, qualification, term, removal

s: The Attorney General is consulted through the Ministry of Law primarily on:
o: All administrative matters of the Union Government
x: References to the Attorney General are made through the Ministry of Law, and consultation is confined to legal matters of real importance.
tq: Watch for the overbroad word 'all' and identify the carefully limited scope of consultation.
sec: Highest law officer of India

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Attorney General — Statutory office; Solicitor General — Constitutional office
Attorney General — Constitutional office under Article 76; Solicitor General — Statutory office
Attorney General — Judicial office under Article 124; Solicitor General — Constitutional office under Article 165
Attorney General — Parliamentary office; Solicitor General — Judicial office
x: The Attorney General is a constitutional authority under Article 76, whereas the Solicitor General is a statutory office.
tq: Separate constitutional and statutory offices before comparing their functions.
sec: Highest law officer of India

s: Which one of the following statements best distinguishes the Solicitor General from the Attorney General?
o: The Solicitor General advises State Governments while the Attorney General advises only courts
The Solicitor General assists the Attorney General and is confined to appearing in courts for the Union
The Solicitor General is the first law officer and the Attorney General is the second law officer
The Solicitor General is the head of the judiciary and the Attorney General assists him
x: The Solicitor General is the second law officer, assists the Attorney General and is confined to appearing in courts for the Union; the Attorney General is the chief legal adviser to the Government of India.
tq: Compare the offices by rank, advisory role and court-related function rather than by title alone.
sec: Highest law officer of India

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary.
2. The Attorney General is a government law officer and the chief legal adviser to the Government of India.
3. The Solicitor General is the second law officer of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The Chief Justice of India heads the judiciary, while the Attorney General and Solicitor General occupy the first and second positions among Union law officers respectively.
tq: Keep the head of the judiciary distinct from the hierarchy of government law officers.
sec: Highest law officer of India

s: The order of precedence assigned to the Attorney General, Solicitor General, and Advocates General is, respectively:
x: The Attorney General is placed at 11, the Solicitor General at 23, and the Additional Solicitors General and Advocates General at 25 in the stated order of precedence.
tq: Read the numerical sequence as an order-of-precedence comparison and avoid reversing the office hierarchy.
sec: Highest law officer of India

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Solicitor General — Second law officer of India
Chief Justice of India — Government's first law officer
Attorney General — Constitutional office under Article 76
Attorney General — Chief legal adviser to the Government of India
x: The Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary, not the government's first law officer. The Attorney General is the chief legal adviser and first law officer of India.
tq: Find the swapped institutional role among closely related constitutional and legal offices.
sec: Highest law officer of India

s:
With reference to the Advocate General of a State, consider the following statements:
1. The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor.
2. The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
3. The remuneration of the Advocate General is determined by the Governor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct under the constitutional arrangement governing the Advocate General of a State.
tq: Use the State-level parallel of the Attorney General arrangement while retaining the Governor as the relevant authority.
sec: Advocate General - appointment, duties, Art. 177, remuneration

s: Under Article 177, the Advocate General of a State may:
o: Speak and take part in the proceedings of either House of the State Legislature and its committees, but not vote
Vote in the State Legislature but not speak in its committees
Dissolve the State Legislature when legal advice is sought
Participate only in the Legislative Assembly and vote in both Houses
x: Article 177 permits the Advocate General to speak and take part in either House of the State Legislature and its committees, but does not confer a right to vote.
tq: Separate the right to participate from the right to vote, a standard constitutional distinction.
sec: Advocate General - appointment, duties, Art. 177, remuneration

s: Which Article provides that the Advocate General enjoys the privileges of a member of the State Legislature?
x: Article 194(4) extends legislative privileges to the Advocate General in the State Legislature. Article 105(4) performs the corresponding function for the Attorney General at the Union level.
tq: Distinguish the participation article from the legislative-privileges article and separate Union from State provisions.
sec: Advocate General - appointment, duties, Art. 177, remuneration

s: The right of audience of the Advocate General extends to:
o: Only the High Court of the State
x: The Advocate General has the right of audience in any court within the State. The Attorney General has the corresponding right of audience in all courts in India.
tq: Use the territorial scope of the office to distinguish the State law officer from the Union law officer.
sec: Advocate General - appointment, duties, Art. 177, remuneration

s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

a. Attorney General — Article 76
b. Advocate General — Article 165
c. Attorney General's parliamentary rights — Article 88
d. Advocate General's State Legislature rights — Article 177
x: The correct matching is Attorney General—Article 76, Advocate General—Article 165, Attorney General's parliamentary rights—Article 88, and Advocate General's State Legislature rights—Article 177.
tq: Start with the sure Article-office pairs and then verify the corresponding legislative-rights provisions.
sec: State-level counterpart of the Attorney General

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Attorney General and the Advocate General:
1. The Attorney General is qualified to be a Supreme Court Judge, whereas the Advocate General is qualified to be a High Court Judge.
2. The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President, whereas the Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
3. The remuneration of both offices is determined by the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the Attorney General's remuneration is determined by the President, while the Advocate General's remuneration is determined by the Governor.
tq: Compare corresponding entries row by row and detect the reversed authority in the remuneration row.
sec: State-level counterpart of the Attorney General

s:
Arrange the following Attorneys General of India in chronological order of holding office, beginning with the earliest:
A. K.K. Venugopal
B. M.C. Setalvad
C. Mukul Rohatgi
D. R. Venkataramani
x: M.C. Setalvad was the first, followed by Mukul Rohatgi, K.K. Venugopal and R. Venkataramani in the sequence represented here.
tq: Fix the first office-holder and then place the later Attorneys General in sequence.
sec: Attorneys General of India → FIRST and current

s: K.K. Venugopal served as the Attorney General of India during which period?
x: K.K. Venugopal served as Attorney General of India from 2017 to 2022.
tq: Treat the paired years as a tenure range and distinguish it from the tenures of neighbouring office-holders.
sec: Attorneys General of India → FIRST and current

s: Who is the Attorney General of India as stated for September 2026?
x: R. Venkataramani is the current Attorney General of India as stated for September 2026. He was first appointed in 2022 and was reappointed for a two-year term in 2025.
tq: Apply the current-affairs date carefully and distinguish the present office-holder from earlier Attorneys General.
sec: Attorneys General of India → FIRST and current

s: R. Venkataramani was first appointed as Attorney General of India in:
x: R. Venkataramani was first appointed Attorney General of India in 2022 and was subsequently reappointed for a two-year term in 2025.
tq: Separate the first appointment year from the later reappointment year.
sec: Attorneys General of India → FIRST and current

s: Under Article 88, the Attorney General may take part in:
o: Only the Lok Sabha and its committees
Either House of Parliament, a joint sitting and committees of which he is named a member
Only the Rajya Sabha and joint sittings
Parliamentary proceedings only after becoming a nominated member
x: Article 88 permits the Attorney General to speak and take part in either House, joint sittings and committees of which he is named a member. This right does not make him a member of Parliament.
tq: Read the full scope of participation and avoid converting a right to attend into membership.
sec: Rights of AG in Parliament - Art. 88; right of audience

s: Which one of the following rights is NOT available to the Attorney General under Article 88?
o: The right to vote in parliamentary proceedings
The right to take part in a joint sitting of Parliament
The right to speak in either House of Parliament
The right to take part in a committee of which he is named a member
x: Article 88 permits participation and speaking but does not confer a right to vote. The Attorney General is not a voting member of Parliament by virtue of that Article.
tq: Find the one power expressly excluded from a broad participation provision.
sec: Rights of AG in Parliament - Art. 88; right of audience

s: The parliamentary privileges of the Attorney General are derived from:
x: Article 105(4) provides the parliamentary privileges applicable to the Attorney General. Article 88 deals with the right to speak and participate without a right to vote.
tq: Distinguish the Article granting participation from the Article extending parliamentary privileges.
sec: Rights of AG in Parliament - Art. 88; right of audience

s: Which Article, among the following, specifically deals with the Attorney General's right to speak and participate in Parliament without voting rights?
x: Article 88 confers the Attorney General's right to speak and take part in parliamentary proceedings without the right to vote. Article 78 concerns the duties of the Prime Minister in relation to the President.
tq: Reject the look-alike Article number and identify the precise constitutional provision.
sec: Rights of AG in Parliament - Art. 88; right of audience

s: Additional Advocates General are appointed primarily to:
o: Replace the Governor in legal matters
Assist the office of the Advocate General
Exercise the voting rights of the Advocate General in the Legislature
Serve as members of the Supreme Court
x: Additional Advocates General assist the office of the Advocate General in discharging its legal responsibilities.
tq: Match the supporting office with its assistance function and avoid assigning it the principal office's constitutional powers.
sec: Advocate General - appointment, duties, Art. 177, remuneration

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional status of the Solicitor General of India?
o: He is a constitutional authority appointed by the President under Article 165
He is a statutory law officer governed by the Law Officers (Terms and Conditions) Rules, 1987
He is created under Article 76 of the Constitution
He is an ex officio member of the Union Cabinet
x: The Solicitor General is not mentioned in the Constitution. The post is statutory and is governed by the Law Officers (Terms and Conditions) Rules, 1987.
tq: Distinguish the constitutional Attorney General from the statutory Solicitor General.
sec: Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Solicitor General of India:
1. He is the second law officer of India.
2. He is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet.
3. His normal term is three years.
4. He is a member of the Union Cabinet.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Solicitor General is the second law officer, is appointed through the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet, and has a three-year term. He is not a member of the Union Cabinet.
tq: Use the membership trap to separate a senior law officer from a Cabinet Minister.
sec: Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General

s: The Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General primarily perform which of the following functions?
o: They conduct elections to Parliament and State Legislatures
They advise the government and appear for the Government of India in courts
They audit the accounts of the Union Government
They preside over joint sittings of Parliament
x: The Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General advise the government and represent the Government of India before courts.
tq: Identify the core function from the office’s legal responsibilities.
sec: Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General

s:
With reference to the law officers of India, consider the following statements:
1. References concerning the Attorney General are made through the Ministry of Law.
2. Law officers conventionally resign when a new government assumes office.
3. The Attorney General alone among these offices is created by the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: References concerning the Attorney General go through the Ministry of Law; law officers conventionally resign after a change of government; and only the Attorney General is constitutionally created, under Article 76.
tq: Combine institutional procedure, convention and constitutional classification.
sec: Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General

s: Tushar Mehta was reappointed as the Solicitor General of India for a period of three years with effect from:
x: Tushar Mehta was reappointed as Solicitor General for three years with effect from 1 July 2026.
tq: Discriminate between closely spaced dates in a current-affairs appointment.
sec: Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General

s: Which of the following persons was NOT included among the five Additional Solicitors General reappointed for the Supreme Court?
x: The five reappointed Additional Solicitors General were Vikramjit Banerjee, K.M. Nataraj, S.V. Raju, N. Venkataraman and Aishwarya Bhati. R. Venkataramani is the Attorney General, not one of those five ASGs.
tq: Find the odd name by checking membership of a specifically stated list.
sec: Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General

s: The Attorney General of India and the Solicitor General of India are ex officio members of the:
x: Under the Advocates Act, 1961, the Attorney General and Solicitor General are ex officio members of the Bar Council of India.
tq: Recall the statutory body associated with the two principal Union law officers.
sec: Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General

s: Which of the following is NOT a permissible activity for the Attorney General of India without the required government permission or contrary to his professional restrictions?
o: Advising the Government of India on legal matters
Engaging in private practice subject to applicable restrictions
Appearing for the Government of India in courts
Defending an accused person in a criminal prosecution
x: The Attorney General must not defend accused persons in criminal prosecutions. He is not a full-time counsel and is not debarred from private practice, but he must comply with restrictions on conflicts and government permission.
tq: Use the exception-based method to separate permitted private practice from prohibited criminal defence.
sec: Limitations on Attorney General

s:
The Attorney General of India must not do which of the following?
1. Advise against the Government of India.
2. Hold a brief against the Government of India.
3. Advise in a case in which he has already advised the Government of India.
4. Become a company director without government permission.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: All four are restrictions applicable to the Attorney General. He must avoid conflicts with the Government of India and cannot become a company director without government permission.
tq: Check each restriction separately, especially the conflict-of-interest and permission clauses.
sec: Limitations on Attorney General

s:
Consider the following statements about the Attorney General of India:
1. He is a full-time counsel of the Union Government.
2. He is a government servant.
3. He is not debarred from private practice merely by holding the office.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Attorney General is neither a full-time counsel nor a government servant. Consequently, he is not debarred from private practice, subject to the restrictions governing the office.
tq: Reject absolute status claims and identify the precise legal position.
sec: Limitations on Attorney General

s: The privileges and immunities available to the Attorney General of India in relation to parliamentary participation are those of:
o: A Union Cabinet Minister under Article 77
A Judge of the Supreme Court under Article 124
A member of a State Legislature under Article 194
A Member of Parliament under Article 105(4)
x: Article 105(4) extends parliamentary privileges and immunities to a person who has the right to speak or otherwise take part in parliamentary proceedings without being a member.
tq: Match the constitutional privilege with the correct article and institutional status.
sec: Limitations on Attorney General

s: A private client asks the Attorney General of India to advise against the Government of India in a matter unrelated to his official duties. Which course is consistent with the limitations on the office?
o: He may do so after obtaining permission from the Chief Justice of India
He may do so because private practice is always unrestricted
He may do so only if the matter is heard outside India
He must decline because he cannot advise or hold a brief against the Government of India
x: Although the Attorney General is not debarred from private practice, he must not advise or hold a brief against the Government of India.
tq: Apply the conflict-of-interest restriction to a practical professional situation.
sec: Limitations on Attorney General

s:
With reference to the Advocate General of Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. The office is provided under Article 165 of the Constitution.
2. The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor of Andhra Pradesh.
3. The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
4. The office necessarily continues unchanged when the State Government changes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Advocate General is a constitutional office under Article 165, appointed by the Governor and holding office at the Governor’s pleasure. By convention, the officeholder may change with the State Government.
tq: Separate constitutional provisions from conventions and test the effect of a change of government.
sec: Advocates General of AP → current holder

s: Which one of the following correctly compares the right of audience of the Attorney General and the Advocate General?
o: The Advocate General has it in all courts in India, while the Attorney General has it only in the State courts
The Attorney General has it in all courts in India, while the Advocate General has it in all courts in the State
Both have it only in the Supreme Court of India
Neither has a right of audience in courts
x: The Attorney General has the right of audience in all courts in India, whereas the Advocate General has the right of audience in all courts within the State.
tq: Split the comparison by territorial scope rather than by rank alone.
sec: Limitations on Attorney General

s: Who was the first Solicitor General of India?
x: C.K. Daphtary was the first Solicitor General of India.
tq: Apply the FIRST/LAST approach to closely related law-officer posts.
sec: Universal angles

s:
Arrange the following offices in descending order according to their position in the precedence table, where the smaller item number indicates higher precedence:
A. Solicitor General
B. Advocate Generals of States
C. Attorney General
D. Additional Solicitors General
Select the correct sequence.
x: The Attorney General is at item 11, the Solicitor General at item 23, and the Advocate Generals of States and Additional Solicitors General are at item 25. Thus the order is Attorney General, Solicitor General, Advocate Generals of States, Additional Solicitors General.
tq: Convert precedence numbers into an ordered sequence and check the tied item number.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which one of the following statements best reflects the criticism of the convention concerning the resignation of law officers when a new government assumes office?
o: It is criticised for linking the offices too closely with the ruling party
It prevents the Attorney General from appearing in constitutional cases
It makes law officers directly elected representatives of the ruling party
It converts statutory law officers into constitutional authorities
x: The convention is criticised because the resignation of all law officers after a change of government can make the offices appear tied to the ruling party rather than being institutionally independent.
tq: Identify the institutional consequence of a convention rather than a formal constitutional rule.
sec: Universal angles

s: In September 2026, the Supreme Court asked Attorney General R. Venkataramani to relay directions to all Advocates General concerning:
o: Reorganisation of the Bar Council of India
x: The Supreme Court asked Attorney General R. Venkataramani to communicate directions to all Advocates General concerning facilities for senior citizens.
tq: Use the subject of a current judicial direction to identify the correct issue.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which of the following current officeholder–tenure pairs is correctly matched?
o: R. Venkataramani—reappointed Attorney General for two years
C.K. Daphtary—reappointed Additional Solicitor General for three years
M.C. Setalvad—reappointed Solicitor General for three years from July 2026
Tushar Mehta—reappointed Attorney General for two years
x: R. Venkataramani was reappointed as Attorney General for two years. Tushar Mehta was reappointed as Solicitor General for three years from 1 July 2026.
tq: Match the current officeholder with the correct office and tenure before evaluating the distractors.
sec: Universal angles
